incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Prefill GPU OOM spike on pool-3 (node group gpu-pool-eu-west) — paging @oncall
anna: taking this. any initial customer reports?
david: seeing many containers restart with exit code 137; kernel OOM nearby. logs show repeated prefill for very long prompts.
anna: confirmed. capturing logs + pids. attaching snippets.
anna: ```
2026-03-15T02:12:45Z runtime: prefill: seq_len=8192 model=redwood-13b qtype=fp16
[2026-03-15T02:12:46Z] kill -9 pid=12345 (OOM Killed)
[2026-03-15T02:12:46Z] container exited with code 137
```
chris: hmm, seq_len 8192 is huge. that explains kernel OOM. which route? looks like customer XYZ sending long context.
maria: CX reports slow responses and timeouts for a subset of requests ~2.5k users. CS drafting status.
anna: immediate plan: 1) throttle long-context routes 2) enable fallback model variant 3) cordon problematic node 4) patch runtime to trim prefill tokens.
david: can we flip routing policy to prefer redwood-lite-8bit for heavy requests? that reduces mem by ~40%.
chris: I can add a policy rule: if prefill_tokens > 2048 route to redwood-lite-8bit, temporary. will push via deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: executing rollout: apply routing-policy v3 -> success (3/3 services updated)
anna: rolling; monitoring mem utilization.
sre-bot: metric alert: gpu_mem_used avg across pool-3 decreased from 98% -> 65% post-rollout
anna: good. still seeing a few crashes though; looks like kernel driver reset on one node.
david: logs show CUDA error sequence on node gpu-node-17:
```
E CudaDriver: cuCtxSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (224)
E Container: restarting pod redwood-runtime-abcde due to signal 6
```
chris: cordoned gpu-node-17 and drained pods -> moving traffic away.
anna: applied temporary rate limit to route /v1/generate?context=large -> 10 rps per org
maria: posting update to affected customers: "we're mitigating GPU memory issues, some queries may be slower; working on permanent fix". will post to status page after you approve.
anna: approved. please include that we routed heavy requests to a lower-memory model variant.
maria: done: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2026-03-prefill-oom
chris: proposed runtime change: soft-prefill-trim to 4k tokens (config ENV MAX_PREFILL=4096) and enable kv-eviction for large contexts; can ship as hotfix.
david: I have a minimal patch to trim prefill at the runtime layer; test on canary.
chris: canary rollout started on pool-canary (5 pods)
deploy-bot: canary pass: 5/5 healthy under 30m
anna: canary looks stable. schedule hotfix rollout to pool-3 with 20% incremental traffic.
deploy-bot: hotfix rollout step1 -> 20% -> success
sre-bot: memory pressure alerts suppressed for nodes in hotfix cohort
anna: note—we still need to avoid evicting customer state. hotfix trims prefill before allocating KV cache.
david: patch details: set MAX_PREFILL=4096; if request.prefill_tokens > MAX_PREFILL then trim oldest context tokens and add a flag `prefill_trimmed=true` to logs.
anna: actionable TODOs for next shift:
- monitor for residual kernel resets (chris)
- review long-context customer throttles and consider quota bump requests (maria)
- prod postmortem + telemetry on prefills > 2k (david)
- update docs and SDKs with prefill limits (eng-docs)
chris: I'm taking next on-call shift at 08:00 UTC. handoff: nodes cordoned: gpu-node-17 (drained), policy rollback plan exists. current impact: 0.5% requests degraded, customers XYZ + QRS affected earlier.
anna: handing off. last note: created incident: INC-2026-03-15-PREFILL-OOM. add any new observations there.
maria: added customer notes and sent targeted emails to top 10 affected orgs.
chris: thanks all. :wave:
anna: :thumbsup: closing paging but keeping thread open for follow-ups.
